selected_topic.title: Autopsy: the startup salary that disappeared in a funding winter
selected_topic.description: Case study: equity that was promised on paper and what actually happened when growth stalled.
selected_topic.angle: Dissect an equity grant from promise to outcome, showing where the value went.
selected_topic.hook_direction: Lead with the offer letter figure and end on what it was actually worth.

ranked_candidates.title: Autopsy: the family that spent six figures and saved nothing
ranked_candidates.description: Case study: a household budget post-mortem showing where the money went and which habits were responsible.
ranked_candidates.angle: Autopsy a real budget and expose the two decisions that consumed the entire year of savings.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Open with the fact that they earned well and still have nothing, then ask how.

ranked_candidates.title: The expense that quietly eats 40% of an average salary
ranked_candidates.description: Silent wealth killer: one recurring household line that leaves almost nothing behind, costed out in yearly and lifetime terms.
ranked_candidates.angle: Treat a single recurring expense as an unseen leak draining the paycheck in real time.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Open by revealing the lifetime total of a cost the owner pays without ever multiplying it out.

ranked_candidates.title: Autopsy: the startup salary that disappeared in a funding winter
ranked_candidates.description: Case study: equity that was promised on paper and what actually happened when growth stalled.
ranked_candidates.angle: Dissect an equity grant from promise to outcome, showing where the value went.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Lead with the offer letter figure and end on what it was actually worth.

ranked_candidates.title: The skill ladder behind a second income
ranked_candidates.description: Asymmetric upside: how one narrow, learnable skill can be sold repeatedly while a salary stays intact.
ranked_candidates.angle: Show the bounded downside of a side skill against the open-ended upside of sellable work.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Contrast the worst case of trying it with the best case, then let the asymmetry speak.

ranked_candidates.title: Why starting to invest at 22 beats starting at 32
ranked_candidates.description: Case study: the same monthly contribution made ten years apart, and the gap that only shows up at retirement.
ranked_candidates.angle: Two identical contributions, two radically different outcomes, with the arithmetic made visible.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Start with the number that ends the story: how much more the early starter ends up with.

ranked_candidates.title: The 24 hours that reset your entire budget
ranked_candidates.description: Actionable blueprint: a two-part system that makes the first days of the month matter instead of ruining the month.
ranked_candidates.angle: Hand the viewer one concrete payday system to install immediately.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Present the blueprint up front as a single change to try this week.

ranked_candidates.title: Split your paycheck the day you get paid
ranked_candidates.description: Actionable blueprint: a fixed allocation between spending, saving, and investing, done automatically on payday.
ranked_candidates.angle: Offer a single repeatable money move the viewer can automate before the month starts.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Open with the instruction itself: what to do in the first ten minutes after payday.

ranked_candidates.title: Why winners sell too early and losers hold too long
ranked_candidates.description: Money behavior: loss aversion turning ordinary investors into bad decision-makers with their own money.
ranked_candidates.angle: Read the investor's own behavior as the culprit, with a familiar self-inflicted mistake as the evidence.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Ask the audience to guess what their own last trade or sale would have looked like.

ranked_candidates.title: Myth: your employer match is free money you can keep
ranked_candidates.description: Money myth: what an employer match really is, and the vesting rule that decides when it is yours.
ranked_candidates.angle: Correct the 'free money' belief by introducing the vesting condition hidden in plain sight.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Start from the widely repeated claim, then reveal the clause that undercuts it.

ranked_candidates.title: Why your savings account is slowly shrinking
ranked_candidates.description: Silent wealth killer: what inflation does to cash sitting still, told as a losing race between two powers.
ranked_candidates.angle: Show purchasing power being eroded in the background while the account balance still looks healthy.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Lead with the mental image of money melting while the account number stays reassuringly the same.

ranked_candidates.title: What an index fund actually owns
ranked_candidates.description: Plain-language look inside a total-market index fund and why that basket grows on its own.
ranked_candidates.angle: Reveal the invisible contents of a single investment vehicle most people already own.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Ask the audience to picture what they actually own when they 'buy the market'.

ranked_candidates.title: How a raise quietly upgraded your expenses
ranked_candidates.description: Money behavior: lifestyle inflation absorbing an income increase so net wealth never moves.
ranked_candidates.angle: Trace a single raise through spending habits to show where the extra money went.
ranked_candidates.hook_direction: Reveal the raise on a payslip and follow the money as it disappears into the month.

pillar_catalog.label: Wealth Engine (How Money Grows)
pillar_catalog.focus: The mechanisms that compound money: interest, index funds, cashflow, and ownership.
pillar_catalog.guidance: Open on the engine itself. Show the machine that produces the money and then let the viewer see it running.

pillar_catalog.label: Silent Wealth Killers (Why Money Doesn't Grow)
pillar_catalog.focus: Quiet, recurring leaks that drain wealth while the balance still looks fine.
pillar_catalog.guidance: Frame it as a crime scene the owner never noticed. Name the leak, show the evidence, quantify what it cost.

pillar_catalog.label: Psychology of Capital (Mindset & Behavior)
pillar_catalog.focus: Money beliefs and behaviors: loss aversion, status spending, sunk cost, and compounding inertia.
pillar_catalog.guidance: Read the suspect's behavior, not the numbers. Explain the mindset that produced the outcome.

pillar_catalog.label: Tactical Blueprints (What You Can Do)
pillar_catalog.focus: Specific, doable actions the viewer can apply to their own money this week.
pillar_catalog.guidance: Hand the viewer the blueprint. One concrete action, clearly stated.

pillar_catalog.label: Income Expansion & Asymmetric Upside (Building Capital)
pillar_catalog.focus: Ways to grow earning power and capture upside where downside is limited.
pillar_catalog.guidance: Show the asymmetry. Small, bounded downside against large, uncertain upside.

pillar_catalog.label: Financial Autopsies & Real-World Breakdown (Case Studies)
pillar_catalog.focus: Real-world cases, companies, and households dissected to show what actually happened.
pillar_catalog.guidance: Open the case file. Walk through what happened and why the outcome was not what it looked like.

channel.audience: Broad English-speaking audience interested in money and wealth.

mascot.note: Appears alongside the narration as a visual presence. Never speaks and never narrates.
